proposal.root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07) because billing import validation rule BV-17 — deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-13) — misreads firmware v4.2 meters' raw register values (reported in "0.1 m3" units vs plain "m3" for older firmware, E-14) as roughly 10x true consumption, causing the import step to reject these valid, timely-delivered AMI reads as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION and substitute estimates, which accounts for 95.5% (1184/1240) of ESTIMATED-read disputes (E-12) — not field route-completion shortfalls (E-01, superseded by ER-1) or AMI/MDMS delivery failure (only 4.5% NO_READ_RECEIVED per E-12).
proposal.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (SH-CS, CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07).
95.5% (1184/1240) of ESTIMATED-read disputes involve a valid AMI read delivered before cutoff but rejected at import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, not an actually missing read (E-12).
billing-config's validation rule change log shows exactly one substantive change, BV-17 (high-consumption check with no unit scaling), deployed 2026-08-01, matching the surge onset (E-13).
Firmware v4.2 meters (rollout 2026-06) report consumption in register_unit "0.1 m3" while older firmware reports in plain "m3", a scaling mismatch BV-17 does not account for (E-14).
Dispute resolution times remain within the 3.0-day SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d, E-02) and no tariff changes occurred (E-03), ruling out slow handling or rate changes as drivers.
causal_chain: Firmware v4.2 AMI meters (rollout 2026-06) report consumption in register_unit "0.1 m3" while older firmware v3.x meters report in plain "m3" (E-14).
On 2026-08-01, billing import validation rule BV-17 was deployed, comparing raw register values directly against 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling "none" (E-13).
For v4.2 meters, BV-17's unscaled comparison interprets raw values as roughly 10x true m3 consumption, flagging them as high-consumption.

The billing import step rejects these flagged reads with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION even though a valid AMI read was delivered before cutoff and exported to billing (E-12: 1184/1240 = 95.5% of ESTIMATED-read disputes).
Rejected reads are substituted with ESTIMATED reads, which customers dispute as inaccurate bills.
This produces the Aug 2026 surge in dispute tickets (E-07: ~600/month to ~1180-1260/month), timed with BV-17's 2026-08-01 deployment (E-13).

assumptions.statement: CRM dispute ticket counts (E-07) capture essentially all billing-related complaints for the period, with no significant off-channel disputes skewing the measured surge.

proposal.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) requested an AI agent to auto-answer billing disputes and "fix wrong bills" after ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month to ~1180-1260/month starting August 2026 (E-07). Investigation determined the real problem (PD-1, superseding an invalidated earlier version PD-1@v1 after E-12 contradicted it): billing import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-13), misreads firmware v4.2 meters' raw register values (reported in "0.1 m3" vs plain "m3" for older firmware, E-14) as roughly 10x true consumption. This causes valid, on-time AMI reads to be wrongly rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION and replaced with estimates, explaining 95.5% (1184/1240) of ESTIMATED-read disputes (E-12, corroborated independently by E-15, E-16, E-17). Response speed (E-02, within SLA) and tariff changes (E-03, zero records) were ruled out as causes; field staffing/route completion (E-01, E-05) was initially suspected but shown by E-12 to not be the mechanism for the ESTIMATED-read disputes. The release decision is HOLD: a release-blocking verification obligation (VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-MECHANIS) asking whether BV-17 also explains the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputes (E-04) remains OPEN, and Layer 1 safety/verification could not be established due to this missing correlation (1190 missing per recent_events seq 354/358). No bill writes or route pushes were made; those protected actions remain gated by K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH respectively.
key_points: Problem as finally defined (PD-1@v2): BV-17, a high-consumption import check deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-13), misinterprets v4.2 meters' '0.1 m3' register units as 10x true consumption (E-14), causing valid AMI reads to be rejected (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) and estimate-substituted, accounting for 95.5% (1184/1240) of ESTIMATED-read disputes (E-12).

The original request framing (CL-01, SH-CS: build an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and fix wrong bills) was treated as an unverified stakeholder claim, not the problem itself; H-RESPONSE-AUTOMATION-GAP was REJECTED because ticket response times were within SLA (E-02).

An earlier problem definition (PD-1@v1), which held that most disputes involved ACTUAL reads and were separate from a field-route issue, was INVALIDATED when E-12 showed the ESTIMATED-read disputes were themselves import-rejection driven, not field-driven (ER-1, ER-2); this cascaded to invalidate related hypotheses, assumptions, remedies, and work items per DR-1.

Competing hypotheses were tested and rejected: AMI/MDMS delivery failure (H-AMI-MDMS-READ-FAILURE, contradicted by E-04/E-12/E-13/E-15/E-17), field read degradation and staffing shortage (H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION, H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE, contradicted by E-04), and response-speed problem (H-RESPONSE-AUTOMATION-GAP, contradicted by E-02).

The correlation and corrected ticket-response-template work (W-WI-CORRELATE-ACTUAL-READ, W-WI-DRAFT-TICKET-RESPONSE, W-WI-MDMS-DEEP-CHECK) was scoped under SD-2/PLAN-2 within release_scope: correlate_import_rejection_with_actual_read_disputes and draft_dispute_ticket_response_update on DA-BILL/DA-TICKET.

Release decision is HOLD because verify_completed (seq 354) reported Layer 1 failed with 'missing:actual_read_dispute_import_correlation: 1190 missing', and VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-MECHANIS (required BEFORE_RELEASE, HIGH impact) is still OPEN, blocking refer_billing_rule_defect_to_billing_ops and analyze_disputed_bills_by_read_type pre-release.

No automated bill writes or route pushes occurred; K-BILLWRITE (requires Billing Operations authority) and K-DISPATCH (requires SH-FIELD runtime confirmation) remain intact and unviolated per the release scope.
limitations_explained: Whether BV-17's unit-scaling defect also explains the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputes (E-04) is unresolved; this is the specific gap that triggered the HOLD decision.

Referring the billing rule defect to Billing Operations and analyzing disputed bills by read type are withheld from this release because the OPEN, HIGH-impact VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-MECHANIS blocks them pre-release.

Actual deployment of a corrected BV-17 rule and manual re-bill/credit execution (remedies SR-R1/SR-R2) fall outside this harness's tool surface and contest time window and cannot be done by this release.

Two unknowns remain OPEN and unaddressed: U-FIELD-COMPLETION-GAP-CAUSE (MEDIUM, whether the field route-completion shortfall has a staffing or other cause) and U-BASELINE-VALIDITY (LOW, whether the pre-August dispute baseline was itself already clean).
Draft dispute-ticket response templates produced by this release cannot auto-send corrections to customers; each batch still requires SH-CS sign-off.
The DEFINE gate for this problem was only a CONDITIONAL_PASS, with deferred items tracked as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than fully closed before proceeding.
